objectives: State what forces do and measure them in newtons.

blocks.title: Force
blocks.md: A **force** is a push or a pull. Its unit is the **newton (N)**, measured with a **spring balance (newton meter)**. A force can start or stop motion, change speed or direction, or change the shape of an object. **Balanced forces** do not change the motion of an object; **unbalanced forces** do.

blocks.caption: Forces on a box pushed along a table.
blocks.alt: A box with arrows: push to the right, friction to the left, weight downward and the reaction of the table upward.

blocks.title: Friction
blocks.md: **Friction** is a force that opposes motion between surfaces in contact. It is useful for walking, braking and gripping tyres. It is harmful when it wears parts and makes heat. It is **reduced** by oil, grease, polishing, wheels and ball bearings; it is **increased** by rough surfaces and treaded tyres.

blocks.title: Mass and weight
blocks.md:
**Mass** is the amount of matter in an object: kg, the same everywhere. **Weight** is the pull of gravity on it: newtons, and it changes with place (on the Moon about one sixth of that on Earth).

**W = m × g**, with **g = 10 N/kg** on Earth (used in this course).

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Mass is not weight: a 60 kg student has a mass of 60 kg and a weight of 600 N.
- A balance measures mass; a spring balance measures weight (force).
- Friction does not always slow things: without it you could not walk.

blocks.title: Speed
blocks.md: **Speed = distance ÷ time**, so **distance = speed × time** and **time = distance ÷ speed**. Units: m/s or km/h. **Average speed = total distance ÷ total time**. To change units: **km/h ÷ 3.6 = m/s** and m/s × 3.6 = km/h.

blocks.caption: Distance-time graph of a bus journey (illustrative numbers).
blocks.alt: A graph with time in hours on the x-axis and distance in km on the y-axis: a rising line to 100 km at 2 h, a flat part until 2.5 h and a rising line to 200 km at 4 h.

blocks.title: Reading the graph
blocks.md: On a **distance-time graph** the **slope** is the speed. A **straight rising line** means constant speed; a **steeper line** means faster; a **horizontal line** means stopped. In the graph above: 0 to 2 h: 100 km in 2 h = 50 km/h; 2 to 2.5 h: stopped; 2.5 to 4 h: 100 km in 1.5 h ≈ 66.7 km/h.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Use matching units: do not divide km by seconds without converting.
- A flat line on a distance-time graph means the object is **stopped**, not moving at constant speed.
- Average speed is total distance ÷ total time, **not** the average of two speeds when times differ.

blocks.title: Average speed
blocks.statement: In the journey of the graph the bus travels 200 km in 4 h including the stop. Find the average speed.
steps: Average speed = total distance ÷ total time.

blocks.title: Change units
blocks.statement: A motorbike travels at 72 km/h. Express this in m/s.
